facts.text: Golden was the first gold rush west of the Mississippi River, predating California's 1849 rush.
Two mining camps, El Real de San Francisco and Placer del Tuerto, merged by 1839 to form Golden, blending Native American, Spanish colonial, and American mining heritage.
The San Francisco Catholic Church, founded in 1839, was restored in 1960 by Fray Angelico Chavez and remains Golden’s most photographed building.
Golden sits along the Turquoise Trail Scenic Byway, about ten miles north of the Sandia Park junction on NM‑14.
The Golden General Merchandise Store, opened in 1918, is the only business still operating in town and is locally known as the Henderson Store.
Before American settlers, the area that became Golden was inhabited by Native Americans and Spaniards, with early Pueblo settlements along Tuerto Creek.
